When SpaceX wasn't recovering rockets, it was actually busy signing deals with AI companies. In February this year, Starlink's parent company brought xAI (which also owns the rebranded X, formerly Twitter) under its umbrella. In April, SpaceX signed an agreement with Cursor, which competes with Claude Code (by Anthropic) and OpenAI's Codex. As of August 14, the acquisition has been completed. And SpaceXAI (the company's new name) has also recently launched the Grok Bot and Grok 4.6 model with Cursor's assistance.

Updated August 14, 2026: SpaceXAI has completed its acquisition of Cursor.

Updated June 16, 2026: SpaceX acquired Cursor one week after becoming a publicly listed company.

Below is an updated version of the original report:

SpaceX strikes $10 billion deal with Cursor ahead of $60 billion acquisition

Cursor has long been popular among software engineers who use Macs for AI-assisted coding. It was one of the earliest services to integrate large language model AI into the application development workflow.

In April this year, SpaceX and Cursor said the two companies were "working closely together to create the world's top coding and knowledge work AI."

The original collaboration included SpaceX paying Cursor $1 billion:

Cursor, in April—before the acquisition was completed—further disclosed details of the collaboration arrangement:

Cursor is partnering with SpaceX to accelerate our model training work. We launched Composer less than six months ago as our first agentic coding model. Subsequently, Composer 1.5 scaled reinforcement learning by more than 20x. Composer 2 further added continued pre-training to achieve frontier-level performance at a fraction of the cost of other models. Each increase in compute has translated into significant improvements in model capability. We have always wanted to push our training work further, but have been constrained by compute bottlenecks. Through this partnership, our team will leverage xAI's Colossus infrastructure to significantly advance our models' intelligence.

The SpaceX-Cursor collaboration further strengthens a product capable of competing with Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex agentic coding software.
